Issues.Title: Kill Windows watch process descendants during forced termination
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
## Summary

Force-kill the entire Windows process tree when `dotnet watch` cannot terminate a process gracefully, instead of killing only the parent. Graceful Ctrl+Break behavior, cleanup deadlines, and Unix handling are unchanged. The force-only helper-process path also benefits.

Add a deterministic parent/child regression covering helper processes and user applications that ignore Ctrl+Break. Surviving children are explicitly cleaned up when running the negative control. Document the invariant in the watch area guidance.

Relates to #40074, not a blanket fix for its generic timeout signature.

## Evidence and limits

[Build 1680545](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1680545) for #57111 has a [Windows watch console](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/ce0b303c-190a-48b7-9106-cc7bbb567587/workitems/dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.7/console) showing the net9 PublishAot test observed ENC0097, watch force-killed `dotnet run` PID 2776 after a 5-second graceful deadline, and its subsequent rebuild failed MSB3027/MSB3021 because the apphost remained locked (reported owner `System (4)`). The test then waited indefinitely for `<updated>`.

The new regression independently proves the parent-only-kill orphaning defect. The console does not prove that an orphan caused that particular System-owned lock; this PR fixes the confirmed cleanup gap without claiming a complete root-cause proof for the CI occurrence or changing #57111's publishing code.

## Validation

- Built the changed watcher and full Debug redist layout with the pinned SDK; stopped remaining unrelated test-project builds after redist completed, so this was not a completed full-repository build.
- Diagnostic-preserving `scripts/RunTests.cs`: termination tests plus all four `ChangeFileInAotProject_PriorNet11` cases, repeated twice. Each run passed 8 and skipped the Unix-only case, including graceful Windows console/WinExe shutdown.
- Reverting only whole-tree Kill to parent-only Kill makes both new regression cases fail because the child remains alive.
- Restored the fix and repeated both new cases twice: all pass.
- Initial WinExe validation needed missing WindowsDesktop runtime `12.0.0-alpha.1.26528.111`; installed it into the private bootstrap layout and reran successfully. No global installation or manifest changes.
- TRX/binlogs retained; patch whitespace and area documentation links checked.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Kill Windows watch process descendants during forced termination" (#57113)

Issues.Title: Report missing inputs for no-build single-file publishing
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
## Summary

Report a localized, actionable error when `publish --no-build` is missing an input to single-file bundling, rather than retrying and failing with an unexpected `GenerateBundle` exception.

The check is immediately before `GenerateBundle`, after the bundle-input extension points have run, and examines the actual `FilesToBundle` items. It does not compare build and publish properties, perform a fallback build, or change ordinary publishing. In particular, enabling `PublishSingleFile` only at publish time remains supported when the required build inputs exist.

Relates to #37367 and #17526. The original host-only transition was already addressed by #37114; this change improves the remaining missing-input diagnostic rather than claiming to fix every build/publish property mismatch.

## Changes

- Add `NETSDK1247` with the missing file's full path and guidance to build with appropriate inputs or omit `--no-build`.
- Add self-contained and framework-dependent missing-assembly regression cases; extend the existing no-build host-switch test to both modes.
- Regenerate the 13 localization files through the normal build tooling.

## Validation

- Built `Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.csproj` for its declared `net12.0` and `net472` targets with SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26523.103`, `/m:1`, and no shared compilation: no warnings or errors.
- Four focused `Microsoft.NET.Publish.Tests` cases pass: missing intermediate assembly and publish-only single-file host switching, each self-contained and framework-dependent. Both missing-input cases fail with the original `MSB4018` when only the target check is reverted, and all four pass after restoring it.
- A separate clean 11-case reproduction run completes 27 restore/build/publish commands with no unexpected exits: the original recipe, explicit missing-RID output, publish-only profile, mismatched configuration, and mismatched TFM produce `NETSDK1247` rather than `MSB4018`; matched SC/FDD, host-only switching, matched profile, matched TFM, and ordinary no-build publishing succeed, and all six published executables run with the expected output.
- The task build regenerated all 13 translation entries in `new` state.

The local product under test was an explicit **source-task/targets overlay**, not a full redist build: the pinned bootstrap SDK supplied the CLI, MSBuild, compiler, and runtime, with the freshly built task assembly and current source SDK targets overlaid. The focused tests used the repository's diagnostic-preserving runner in a private copy adding serialization arguments; the existing test-root setup targets supplied the normal isolation files. Full redist and native CI validation remain for PR CI.

Issues.Title: Fix flaky cross-entry-point telemetry drain lease assertion
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
## Summary

`PersistentStorageTelemetryE2ETests.ItDrainsTelemetryPersistedByTheOtherEntryPoint` still flakes after #57018. It failed on #56972 ([build 1680043](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1680043), `dotnet.Tests.dll.19`, Windows x64) with a different assertion. The writer's blob was still `.blob`, not `.lock`. The AOT drainer (`dotnet solution list`) exited after 538 ms without leasing the blob.

In Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter 1.10.0, the lease happens on background threads. Those threads are the eager drain, which starts 50 ms after startup, and the shutdown drain. Shutdown starts the drain without waiting for it to finish. `PersistThenDrain` also uses part of the CLI's 300 ms error-exit budget to persist the drainer's own telemetry before the drain gets the remainder. On a slow machine, the process can exit before any lease happens.

The test now runs the drainer up to 5 times and stops after the writer's blob is leased. The contract is still checked: if the entry points don't share a storage directory, the blob never gets leased. Production behavior doesn't change.

## Validation

- Ran `scripts\RunTests.cs` for `PersistentStorageTelemetryE2ETests` with `--repeat 15`. All 60 test cases passed, with no skips.

Relates to #56957

Issues.Title: dotnetup update should avoid installing older versions when a newer matching version is already installed
Issues.Body:
`dotnetup update` resolves a version from the release manifest and checks whether that exact version is installed. It can unnecessarily install an older version even when a newer, locally installed version already satisfies the requirement.

For example:
- A registered `global.json` permits major-version roll-forward and prereleases.
- .NET SDK 12 is installed and tracked, but isn’t yet in the release index.
- The latest matching version available through the release index is .NET SDK 11.

Updating that repository requirement should retain SDK 12 without downloading SDK 11.  Current behavior would be to install the latest .NET 11 SDK that is in the release manifest.

Update should compare the manifest candidate against the newest valid, tracked installation satisfying the same requirement in the same root and architecture. Reuse the matching semantics used by list and garbage collection, including minimum-version and prerelease constraints. A separate stable-only `latest` spec may still legitimately require SDK 11 when SDK 12 is a prerelease.

Include regression coverage for newer matching installations, invalid or missing local installations, and stable-only requirements. Define how selecting an existing local version interacts with `--update-global-json`.

Related discussion: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56798#discussion_r4458766020
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "dotnetup update should avoid installing older versions when a newer matching version is already installed" (#57102)

Issues.Title: CA2012 false positive when a ValueTask-returning query expression is returned or awaited
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When a type implements the LINQ query pattern with methods that return `ValueTask<T>`, CA2012 reports the outermost query operator call. This happens even when the query's result is returned directly or awaited directly. The same code in method syntax doesn't warn.

The cause seems to be that, in the `IOperation` tree, the outermost `Select/SelectMany` invocation sits under an `ITranslatedQueryOperation`. The analyser doesn't look through that node, so it never sees the parent `IReturnOperation` / `IAwaitOperation` and treats the result as consumed some other way.

This is separate from #56983 *(receivers of C# 14 extension block members)*. The repro below only uses classic extension methods.

### Steps to reproduce

SDK 11.0.100, net10.0, `<AnalysisLevel>latest-Minimum</AnalysisLevel>`

```
public static class ValueTaskQueryExtensions
{
    public static async ValueTask<TResult> Select<T, TResult>(
        this ValueTask<T> source, 
        Func<T, TResult> selector)
        => selector(await source);

    public static async ValueTask<TResult> SelectMany<T, TMiddle, TResult>(
        this ValueTask<T> source,
        Func<T, ValueTask<TMiddle>> collectionSelector,
        Func<T, TMiddle, TResult> resultSelector)
    {
        T value = await source;
        return resultSelector(value, await collectionSelector(value));
    }
}

public static class Repro
{
    static ValueTask<int> GetAsync() => ValueTask.FromResult(42);

    // No warning:
    public static ValueTask<int> MethodSyntax() 
        => GetAsync().SelectMany(a => GetAsync(), (a, b) => a + b);

    // CA2012:
    public static ValueTask<int> QueryReturned() 
        => from a in GetAsync() 
           from b in GetAsync() 
           select a + b;

    // CA2012:
    public static async Task<int> QueryAwaited() 
        => await (from a in GetAsync() 
                  from b in GetAsync() 
                  select a + b);

    // CA2012:
    public static ValueTask<int> QuerySelectOnly() 
        => from a in GetAsync() 
           select a * 2;
}
```

### Expected behavior

No CA2012. The `ValueTask` produced by the query is returned or awaited directly, the same as in `MethodSyntax`.

### Actual behavior

CA2012 is reported on the last query clause (the `from b ...` clause, or the `select` clause in QuerySelectOnly) for all three query forms.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Are there any workarounds?

Suppress the warning, or rewrite everything to use method syntax.

Issues.Title: Run GenerateAssemblyInfo before XamlPreCompile
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/msbuild#15040
Fixes #51159
Related: #17890 (same root cause, CA1416 / `SupportedOSPlatformAttribute`)

## Problem
`XamlPreCompile` (defined in MSBuild's `Microsoft.CSharp.CurrentVersion.targets`) is a copy of `CoreCompile` that XAML tooling such as WinUI runs during `PrepareResources`. That is before `BeforeCompile` and `CoreCompile`. `GenerateAssemblyInfo` is hooked only to `BeforeCompile;CoreCompile`, so it has not run when `XamlPreCompile` compiles.

Assembly attributes generated from project properties are therefore missing in that compile pass (`DisableRuntimeMarshalling`, `SupportedOSPlatform`, ...). In a WinUI project with `<DisableRuntimeMarshalling>true</DisableRuntimeMarshalling>`, a `[LibraryImport]` or `[GeneratedComInterface]` member that needs runtime marshalling disabled fails with:

`error SYSLIB1051: Runtime marshalling must be disabled in this project by applying the 'System.Runtime.CompilerServices.DisableRuntimeMarshallingAttribute' to the assembly ...`

Binlog evidence from the repro (https://github.com/dongle-the-gadget/XamlPreCompileRepro): the `GenerateAssemblyInfo` target never runs, and `App1.AssemblyInfo.cs` is not in the `Sources` of the `Csc` task inside `XamlPreCompile`.

## Change
Add `XamlPreCompile` to `BeforeTargets` of `GenerateAssemblyInfo` and update the comment. The existing comment already says this target must run before every compiler invocation.

This was suggested in the discussion: "It would be safer to add `XamlPreCompile` to the `BeforeTargets` for `GenerateAssemblyInfo`" (@dsplaisted, #51159), and earlier in #17890.

## Alternatives considered
- **`XamlPreCompile` depending on `BeforeCompile`** would also fix this and cover other prerequisites. It could break existing builds, though: `BeforeCompile` hooks are user-defined and today run only right before `CoreCompile`. Running them earlier may break hooks that assume the state at that point.
- **`AfterTargets="PrepareForBuild"` on `GenerateAssemblyInfo`** (the abandoned #52223, and suggested in #51159): this moves the target earlier in *every* build, not only those that run `XamlPreCompile`. That PR needed test workarounds (`EnableSourceControlManagerQueries=false`) because source control information is then picked up at a different time. It also risks tools that set version-related properties in a target just before compile. Its test depended on `GenerateAssemblyInfo` from a target hooked before `CoreCompile`, so it passed without the fix.
- **Hooking only `BeforeCompile`**, as done for `AddImplicitDefineConstants` in #44695: it does not help here, because `BeforeCompile` runs after `XamlPreCompile` (see the binlog analysis in #43908).

The trade-off of this change is that other compile prerequisites hooked on `BeforeCompile` still need their own hook for `XamlPreCompile`.

## Validation
- Manual: with a copy of the SDK 10.0.404 `Sdks` folder (`MSBuildSDKsPath`), the WinUI repro and a plain console project both fail with SYSLIB1051 before the change and build successfully after it, including an incremental rebuild. Order in the binlog: `CoreGenerateAssemblyInfo` → `GenerateAssemblyInfo` → `XamlPreCompile` → `CoreCompile`.
- New tests in `GivenThatWeWantToControlGeneratedAssemblyInfo`:
  - `It_generates_assembly_info_before_XamlPreCompile`: runs the real `XamlPreCompile` target during `PrepareResources` (as WinUI does) on a project with a `[LibraryImport]` method taking a `char` and `DisableRuntimeMarshalling=true`. It checks the build passes (no SYSLIB1051, no duplicate attribute), that the final assembly has the attribute, and that an incremental build still works.
  - `It_does_not_generate_assembly_info_for_XamlPreCompile_if_opted_out`: with `GenerateAssemblyInfo=false` no assembly info file is generated.
- Not yet run: the new tests have not been run in the SDK repo's test harness (only the equivalent scenario was run manually, as described above). Only .NET 10.0.404 and x64 were tried. CI will tell.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Run GenerateAssemblyInfo before XamlPreCompile" (#57100)

The runtime package's publishing default is excluded from restore evaluation. Use the existing `RequiresCrossgen2Pack` property to acquire the compiler without setting `PublishReadyToRun` or changing normal-build behavior.

Land this before the companion runtime default. Until that runtime package ships, the SDK may restore an unused compiler for CoreCLR browser projects.

## Validation

Final same-selector controls for the two new methods/seven rows: original SDK target, 6 passed and one expected missing-default dependency assertion failure; changed SDK target, 7 passed, zero failed/skipped. Both runs inherited a matching workload-pack root and the test cleared it. The generated target was restored exactly; the existing compiler package's bytes/types/permissions were unchanged.

With the companion runtime patch, 13 property cases, 3 fresh restore controls and 24 browser cases passed. In-tree library runs passed 32 tests in each mode. The full SDK build failed on unrelated EmptyFiles copies in developer tools; the complete product-redist build passed. CI, installed-workload execution and performance benchmarks were not run.

Issues.Title: Fix dotnet-new template samples test and dotnet-watch .slnx sharing violation
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
This PR combines two independent CI fixes so they can be reviewed and merged together. CI build [1678390](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1678390) passed with both changes applied.

- **Part 1** (first three commits, previously #57078): test the in-repo template engine samples instead of the published package. Fixes #57031.
- **Part 2** (last commit): release the generated `.slnx` write handle in `dotnet-watch` before building. Fixes #57065.

Fixes #57031
Fixes #57065

---

## Part 1: Test the in-repo template engine samples instead of the published package

`TemplateEngineSamplesTest` installed the latest *published* `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples` package, so publishing `11.0.100` (which drops `FSharp.NET.Sdk` from the F# sample) broke the checked-in `sample06 --language F#` snapshot.

The samples live in this repo (`documentation/TemplateEngine/Samples`), so the test now uses them directly instead of any package:

- `Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Samples.csproj` marks its template content `CopyToOutputDirectory` (linked under `TemplateEngineSamples/`). The package layout is unchanged (verified the nupkg entries are identical).
- `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests.csproj` has a `ProjectReference` (`ReferenceOutputAssembly="false"`) to the samples project, so building the tests copies the templates into the test output.
- `TemplateEngineSamplesTest` installs the `TemplateEngineSamples` folder from its output directory.
- The F# snapshot is updated to the in-repo sample (plain `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`, no legacy package references).

Snapshots now always match the template content in the same commit.

Validated locally: all 16 `TemplateEngineSamplesTest` cases pass.

---

## Part 2: Release the generated `.slnx` write handle before building

### Root cause

Commit 2133b177c8f ("Create dotnet-watch solution files privately") changed `dotnet-watch` to keep the generated multi-project `.slnx` open with `FileAccess.ReadWrite` + `FileShare.Read` for the duration of the build. MSBuild's solution parser (`Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence`) opens the file with `File.OpenRead`, which requests `FileShare.Read`; Windows denies that open while another handle holds write access. From the Helix console of the failing runs:

```
aspire watch server ❌ ...\dotnet-watch-h42e2re5.vgl\1.slnx : error MSB4025: The project file could not be loaded. System.IO.IOException: The process cannot access the file '...\1.slnx' because it is being used by another process.
   at System.IO.File.OpenRead(String path)
   at Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence.Serializer.SingleFileSerializerBase`1...OpenAsync(...)
   at Microsoft.Build.Construction.SolutionFile.ParseUsingNewParser()
```

The initial build of the Aspire watch server failed, so `AspireLauncherIntegrationTests.ServerAndResources` waited for `Capabilities` output that never came until the test host was killed (hang dumps of `Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire` / `dotnet`). Any `dotnet watch` session that builds multiple projects through a generated solution on Windows hits the same build failure. The existing unit test masked the bug by reading with `FileShare.ReadWrite` instead of `File.OpenRead`.

### Fix

`TemporaryFileManager.Create` now takes a content writer: it writes through an exclusive handle, closes it, and then keeps only a read-only, `FileShare.Read` handle open until disposal. Readers using `File.OpenRead` succeed, while the file still can't be modified or deleted during the build (and stays in the owner-only private directory). `TemporaryFile` exposes `Path` instead of the underlying stream, so callers can't use a closed or read-only stream by mistake.

### Validation

- `TemporaryFileManagerTests` now reads via `File.OpenRead` (what MSBuild uses) and, on Windows, asserts that write access is still denied.
- Ran `TemporaryFileManagerTests` + `AspireLauncherIntegrationTests` locally on Windows against a rebuilt redist layout: 3/3 passed, and the server log shows `Build succeeded: ...\1.slnx`.

Note: #57066 (draft, Copilot coding agent) addresses the same `dotnet-watch` issue by reopening the handle at the call site; this PR instead makes the helper API safe by construction. Only one of the two should be merged.

Issues.Title: SDK 11.0.100: SIGTERM sent to `dotnet <local-tool>` / `dotnet tool run` is not forwarded to the tool; the tool is orphaned (regression from 10.0.x, NativeAOT CLI path)
Issues.Body:
### Description

With SDK 11.0.100 on Linux, sending SIGTERM to `dotnet <toolcommand>` (or `dotnet tool run <toolcommand>`) kills the `dotnet` process at once. The tool process is never signalled. It is reparented to init/the subreaper and keeps running. With SDK 10.0.403, the same SIGTERM is forwarded to the tool by `ProcessReaper`, and both processes exit.

Setting `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0` with SDK 11.0.100 restores the SDK 10 behaviour.

Context: we hit this in a CLI that runs as a local tool and starts `dotnet watch` and a dev server, which process managers stop with SIGTERM.

### Environment

- Linux x64 (NixOS 26.11, kernel 7.3, glibc 2.44)
- SDK 11.0.100 (commit `297acf930f`), host/runtime 11.0.0. This is the official `dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-linux-x64.tar.gz`, SHA-512 verified against `release-metadata/11.0/releases.json`.
- SDK 10.0.403 (commit `5a2162bea6`), host/runtime 10.0.14, for comparison.

### Repro

`sigtool/sigtool.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <!-- lets the same package run on SDK 10 or on SDK 11 alone -->
    <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
    <PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>
    <ToolCommandName>sigtool</ToolCommandName>
    <PackageId>SigTool</PackageId>
    <Version>1.0.0</Version>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

`sigtool/Program.cs`:

```csharp
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

string log = args.Length > 0 ? args[0] : "sigtool.log";
void Log(string s) => File.AppendAllText(log, $"{DateTime.UtcNow:HH:mm:ss.fff} {s}\n");

Log($"pid {Environment.ProcessId} ppid {File.ReadAllText("/proc/self/stat").Split(' ')[3]}");
using var term = PosixSignalRegistration.Create(PosixSignal.SIGTERM, _ => Log("got SIGTERM"));
using var intr = PosixSignalRegistration.Create(PosixSignal.SIGINT, _ => Log("got SIGINT"));
Thread.Sleep(Timeout.Infinite);
```

Pack it and install it as a local tool:

```sh
dotnet pack sigtool -c Release -o feed
mkdir use && cd use
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install SigTool --add-source ../feed
```

Start the tool with `dotnet` as session leader and send SIGTERM to the `dotnet` process only (from `use/`):

```sh
log=$PWD/sig.log; rm -f "$log"
setsid dotnet sigtool "$log" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
leader=$!
until [ -s "$log" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
tool=$(awk '/pid/{print $3; exit}' "$log")
ps -o pid=,ppid=,args= -g "$leader"
kill -TERM "$leader"; wait "$leader"; echo "dotnet exit status: $?"
sleep 3
if kill -0 "$tool" 2>/dev/null; then echo "tool ALIVE, ppid $(ps -o ppid= -p "$tool")"; else echo "tool exited"; fi
cat "$log"
kill -KILL "$tool" 2>/dev/null
```

Replace `dotnet sigtool` with `dotnet tool run sigtool` to check the other form.

### Expected (SDK 10.0.403)

`dotnet` forwards SIGTERM to the tool, and both exit. This happened in 3/3 runs of `dotnet sigtool` and in `dotnet tool run sigtool`:

```
dotnet exit status: 143
tool exited
19:05:16.390 pid 1001163 ppid 1001151
19:05:16.571 got SIGTERM
```

### Actual (SDK 11.0.100)

`dotnet` dies about 15 ms after the signal. The tool never receives SIGTERM, is reparented (here to `systemd --user`, the subreaper) and keeps running. This happened in 3/3 runs of `dotnet sigtool` and in `dotnet tool run sigtool`:

```
dotnet exit status: 143
tool ALIVE, ppid 1593        # systemd --user
19:07:54.527 pid 1003745 ppid 1003736
                              # no "got SIGTERM"
```

With `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0` and SDK 11.0.100, the tool logs `got SIGTERM` and exits, as with SDK 10.

`/proc/<dotnet pid>/status` shows that the SDK 11 `dotnet` process (which has `libdotnet-aot.so` mapped and no `libcoreclr.so`) does not catch SIGTERM:

| | `SigCgt` | SIGTERM (bit 15) caught? |
|---|---|---|
| SDK 10.0.403 `dotnet sigtool` | `00000003000344fa` | yes |
| SDK 11.0.100 `dotnet sigtool` | `0000000300030482` | no |

SIGINT is unaffected:

- SIGINT to the `dotnet` process alone: both SDKs ignore it, which is the intended `ProcessReaper` behaviour. Neither `dotnet` nor the tool exits, and the tool does not get the signal.
- SIGINT to the whole process group, as Ctrl+C does: on both SDKs the tool gets SIGINT, and `dotnet` exits with status 130.

So interactive Ctrl+C works. Only a signal aimed at the `dotnet` process is affected, such as `kill`, `systemctl stop`, an IDE's stop button, a CI step timeout or a container runtime.

### Regression

This is a regression from SDK 10.0.x. It looks like a reintroduction of dotnet/sdk#50965, which was fixed for SDK 10 by dotnet/sdk#50983, on the new NativeAOT entry point.

### Analysis (suspected cause)

This is based on reading the source at the 11.0.100 build commit (VMR `dotnet/dotnet@297acf930f`; `src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs`, `Program.cs` and `ProcessReaper.cs` are identical on `dotnet/sdk` `release/11.0.1xx`@`2b2b3b81a4`).

1. Since .NET 10 the runtime installs no default SIGTERM handler (dotnet/docs#46226). The managed CLI compensates in `Program.Main` with `PosixSignalRegistration.Create(PosixSignal.SIGTERM, _ => Environment.Exit(0))`. `Environment.Exit` raises `AppDomain.ProcessExit`, where `ProcessReaper` forwards SIGTERM to the child.
   - SDK 10: [`Program.cs#L37-L39`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/5a2162bea6845eabc1fc721624a43568c65db3b1/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet/Program.cs#L37-L39). The reaper subscribes to ProcessExit at [`ProcessReaper.cs#L51`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/5a2162bea6845eabc1fc721624a43568c65db3b1/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L51) and forwards at [`#L167`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/5a2162bea6845eabc1fc721624a43568c65db3b1/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L167).
   - SDK 11 managed CLI, still present: [`Program.cs#L78-L80`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet/Program.cs#L78-L80).
2. In SDK 11 the muxer calls `dotnet_execute` in `libdotnet-aot.so` ([`NativeEntryPoint.cs#L36`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L36)). Its own comment says that "the AOT host does not run Program.Main" ([`#L74-L75`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L74-L75)). Since dotnet/sdk#54810 / #54827, and on by default since #55144, external and local tool commands and `tool run` run inside that AOT process ([`#L239`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L239), [`#L393`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/dotnet-aot/NativeEntryPoint.cs#L393)). `NativeEntryPoint.cs` registers no `PosixSignalRegistration` for SIGTERM.
3. So `ProcessReaper` still subscribes to ProcessExit ([`ProcessReaper.cs#L151-L153`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L151-L153), forwarding at [`#L192`](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f/src/sdk/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Utils/ProcessReaper.cs#L192)). But SIGTERM takes its OS default action, so the process ends without ProcessExit and the child is never signalled. This matches the missing SIGTERM bit in `SigCgt` above, and the fact that `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0`, which goes through the managed `Program.Main`, fixes it.

The open PR dotnet/sdk#56332 adds a `ProcessLifecycle` class with a SIGTERM registration that is used from `NativeEntryPoint`, and may fix this as a side effect. It is not merged or backported to `release/11.0.1xx`. A minimal fix for 11.0.1xx could be to register the same `SIGTERM → Environment.Exit(0)` handler at the start of `NativeEntryPoint.ExecuteCore`. Other in-process AOT paths that start a child with `ProcessReaper`, such as `AotRunCommand` for file-based apps, are probably affected the same way. We have not verified this.

### Impact

IDEs, CI systems, `systemd`, container runtimes and other process managers stop processes with SIGTERM to the PID they started. When that PID is `dotnet <local-tool>`, the tool — and whatever it started, such as `dotnet watch`, dev servers and application hosts — keeps running orphaned, holding ports and file locks. This is the same impact as dotnet/sdk#50965.

### Workarounds

- Set `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=0`.
- In the tool, poll the parent PID and shut down when the `dotnet` process that started it is gone. This is what we do now.
- Send the signal to the whole process group instead of the `dotnet` PID.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "SDK 11.0.100: SIGTERM sent to `dotnet <local-tool>` / `dotnet tool run` is not forwarded to the tool; the tool is orphaned (regression from 10.0.x, NativeAOT CLI path)" (#57091)

Issues.Title: CA2007 does not report `await foreach` over `WithCancellation(...)` without `ConfigureAwait`
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

CA2007 reports an `await foreach` over an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` that has no `ConfigureAwait` call, but not one over `source.WithCancellation(cancellationToken)`. [`WithCancellation`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/313982dff3457c8291e8b88cd99785f6920319f0/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/Tasks/TaskAsyncEnumerableExtensions.cs#L36-L41) creates its `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>` with `continueOnCapturedContext: true`, so that loop resumes on the captured context just like the unconfigured one.

The analyzer [skips any `await foreach` whose collection is a `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/88876b0c0b61b6e0ede17ac8e0ad8c95d3fc346b/src/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers/src/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers/Microsoft.CodeQuality.Analyzers/ApiDesignGuidelines/DoNotDirectlyAwaitATask.cs#L97-L99). `ConfigureAwait(bool)` and `WithCancellation(CancellationToken)` both return that type, so the type alone does not show whether the context was configured.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a class library with `dotnet new classlib --name Repro`, delete `Class1.cs`, and add this `.editorconfig` next to the project file:

```ini
root = true

[*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2007.severity = warning
```

Add `Sample.cs`:

```csharp
namespace Repro;

public static class Sample
{
    public static async Task RunAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<int> source, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await foreach (var item in source) { }
        await foreach (var item in source.WithCancellation(cancellationToken)) { }
        await foreach (var item in source.WithCancellation(cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false)) { }
    }
}
```

Run `dotnet build`.

### Expected behavior

CA2007 reports the first and second loops. The third loop calls `ConfigureAwait(false)`, so it is not reported.

### Actual behavior

CA2007 reports only the first loop:

```text
<repro>/Sample.cs(7,36): warning CA2007: Consider calling ConfigureAwait on the awaited task (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/quality-rules/ca2007)
```

### Is this a regression?

No. The `await foreach` check has skipped `ConfiguredCancelableAsyncEnumerable<T>` collections since dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#6683 added it.

### Are there any workarounds?

Write `.ConfigureAwait(false)` after `WithCancellation(...)` by hand. Nothing reports a loop where it is missing.

### dotnet --info output

Trimmed to the SDK, runtime environment, and host sections:

```console
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            297acf930f
 Workload version:  11.0.100-manifests.08e30c08
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26529.118+297acf930

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     ubuntu
 OS Version:  26.10
 OS Platform: Linux
 RID:         linux-x64
 Base Path:   <dotnet-root>/sdk/11.0.100

Host:
  Version:      11.0.0
  Architecture: x64
  Commit:       297acf930f
```

### IDE version

None; reproduced with `dotnet build`.

### Other details

Telling the two calls apart means looking at the invocation chain that produced the collection, for example whether it contains a `ConfigureAwait` call, rather than at the collection's type.

dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#3703 is related: it asks for CA2007 to cover any type that has a `ConfigureAwait(bool)` method. This report is about a type the rule already handles.

_Drafted by Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)._

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Fix dotnet watch crash after switching target frameworks
Issues.Body:
A MAUI project can target both Windows and Android. Running it on Windows, then Android, then starting `dotnet watch` for Android can make the first C# edit crash with a `NullReferenceException` in Roslyn's `DefinitionMap.GetPreviousMethodHandle`.

Watch prepares compiler inputs for the selected target, but also loaded the other targets into Roslyn. If the earlier Windows build still matched the source, Roslyn tried to update Windows without complete compiler inputs, even though only Android was running.

This change passes the project instances from completed design-time builds to Roslyn, instead of every target in the project graph. It does not depend on C# compiler items, so VB and F# projects are kept too. Referenced projects targeting other frameworks are still included.

The regression test reproduces the crash without MAUI or a device: build another target first, start watch for the selected target, then edit a method. The control case skips the earlier build. All 18 focused tests pass, including source edits in VB and F#, dependencies, and project changes.

Related to https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/79898. This fixes the reproduced cross-target case; I have not confirmed whether it also fixes the empty-update case in that issue.

Issues.Title: Improve SDK task execution with multithreaded MSBuild
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Opt `EnsureHotReloadBrowserToolsKey`, `EnsureHotReloadWebSocketKey`, and `GenerateJSModuleManifest` into in-process multithreaded MSBuild execution, resolving filesystem operands through the injected task environment.
- Coordinate concurrent assets-file and targeting-pack cache initialization per retained engine-owned entry. Preserve build/process lifetimes, retry thrown initialization failures, avoid retaining task factories, and isolate cache entries across SDK assemblies/value types.
- Keep original path inputs for directory validation and key-write control flow. A shared resolver follows the actual host runtime and Framework legacy-path switch, rather than assuming a task's target TFM determines BCL behavior.
- Add concurrency, failure-retry, path-isolation, incrementality, invalid-input, and real-MSBuild mixed-runtime regression coverage. Document explicit redist SDK selection for contributor validation.

## Review follow-ups

Completed three review/fix passes covering cache ownership/concurrency, path/host compatibility, and final regression coverage.

The compatibility pass reproduced five failing cases for whitespace-only parent directories: argument-validation behavior changed and a key task could write the private half before failing. The final pass also reproduced a Framework task loaded by .NET MSBuild selecting the wrong validation policy. Both are fixed and covered by regression tests that failed before the fixes.

No dependency versions, generated output formats, or default non-MT command behavior are intentionally changed.

## Validation

Windows validation used the assembled `12.0.100-dev` redist with MSBuild `18.13.0-1.26528.111`, plus the installed .NET Framework MSBuild `18.13.0-1.26527.1`. Task assemblies were built for `net12.0` and `net472`; deployed DLL hashes were checked against build outputs.

```powershell
.\build.cmd -c Debug /bl:artifacts\log\mt-review-final.binlog

.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- `
  --project test\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests.csproj

.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- `
  --project test\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tests\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tests.csproj `
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~EnsureHotReloadBrowserToolsKeyTest|FullyQualifiedName~GenerateJSModuleManifestMultiThreadingTest" `
  --repeat 2
```

- Full core task suite: **426 passed**.
- Focused SWA coverage: **35 passed**, twice.
- Configured ILLink smoke coverage: **3 passed**, including a successful linked publish and an expected failing publish.
- Composed-product matrix: **25 cases passed** across clean/incremental builds, explicit strict-mode sentinel probes, normal and suppressed execution, empty manifests, expected failure exits, publish exclusions, .NET Framework task/cache execution, and Framework task assemblies hosted by .NET MSBuild. Existing key/manifest bytes and timestamps stayed stable on no-op builds; generated JSON contained no sentinel paths and published output excluded key documents.

The existing pinned `Microsoft.Build.TaskAuthoring.Analyzer` was run without blanket suppressions. Its report-only `MSBuildTask0005` callback-provenance notes and `MSBuildTask0003` invalid-argument validation note were manually traced and covered by the compatibility/strict-mode cases; this is not presented as an analyzer-clean migration.

TRX and build/test binlogs are retained under `artifacts\log\test-runs\`; the composed matrix's commands, expected/actual exit codes, and logs were also retained with the session's reproduction fixture.

**Limitations:** Unix execution was not performed. These changes remove identified redundant work and enable in-process routing; no quantified overall build-time speedup is claimed.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118741 | ASP.NET Core Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120778 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22101 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions) - **MSRC severity:** Important ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120778](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120778) ### Acknowledgements - l8BL with [ENKI WhiteHat](https://enki.co.kr/) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Insecure temporary files used by Aspire CLI can allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive configuration information. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22100 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L` - **Weakness:** CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File) - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Information Disclosure ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire CLI ([Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli)) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected component is the Aspire CLI's deprecated MCP configuration scanner, which ships in the CLI packages listed above. Its temporary-file diagnostics can include configuration content and use a fixed path in a shared temporary directory. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves running Aspire CLI agent or MCP initialization commands on a non-Windows system with a temporary directory shared by multiple users. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22092 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating. Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120006](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120006) ### Acknowledgements - samthewhitehat ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/57040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory. If Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire is restored separately, update its package reference or the consuming tool's version configuration to 10.0.404 or 11.0.100, as applicable, restore the tool, and restart the consuming process. An SDK update alone does not update that restored copy. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114155](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114155) ### Acknowledgements - [Ky0toFu](https://x.com/ky0tofu) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

versions 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128, 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, and 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` are affected when their runtime package version is in the platform-specific ranges above. On Linux, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6 and release candidates 1 through 3. On macOS, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6. Preview 7 is not affected on either platform, and macOS release candidates 1 through 3 are not affected. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? For affected Linux and macOS .NET 11 prereleases, install .NET 11.0.0 or update each independently referenced runtime package to 11.0.0. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. On macOS, `PolicyEnforcement.Always` remains unsupported and throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`. The update prevents authentication from proceeding without the required protection; it does not add Extended Protection support on macOS. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118746](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118746) ### Acknowledgements - Alejandro Pacheco - Anonymous - Markus Magnuson ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: .NET 11 - Release
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10711. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the general availability of .NET 11.

Read about the final release in the [.NET Blog announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/announcing-dotnet-11/).

This release includes C# 15, faster developer tools, runtime and library improvements, and new capabilities for web, mobile, desktop, and AI apps. Explore the full release notes below.

## 🛠️ SDK

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/sdk.md)

## 📱 .NET MAUI

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/dotnetmaui.md)

## 🎁 Entity Framework Core

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/efcore.md)

## 📚 Libraries

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/libraries.md)

## ⏱️ Runtime

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/runtime.md)

## C# 15

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/csharp.md)

## F# 11

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/fsharp.md)

## 🌐 ASP.NET Core & Blazor

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/aspnetcore.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Forms

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/winforms.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/wpf.md)

## 🚀 Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, use an up-to-date [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/) installation that supports .NET 11.

You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Before upgrading an existing application, review the [breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11), update your target frameworks and dependencies, and run your tests.

Celebrate the release of .NET 11 at [.NET Conf 2026](https://dot.net/conf), November 10-13.

## 🔔 Stay up-to-date with .NET 11

You can stay up-to-date with all the features of .NET 11 with:

* [What's new in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/whats-new/dotnet-11/overview)
* [What's new in C# 15](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/whats-new/csharp-15)

* [What's new in ASP.NET Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11)
* [What's new in Aspire](https://aspire.dev/whats-new/)
* [What's new in Entity Framework Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/ef/core/what-is-new/ef-core-11.0/whatsnew)
* [What's new in Windows Forms](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/winforms/whats-new/net110)
* [What's new in WPF](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/whats-new/net110)
* [Breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11)
* [.NET 11 releases](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/README.md)

Be sure to subscribe to the GitHub Discussions [RSS news feed](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/categories/news.atom) for all release announcements.
